q: Mechanisms of breathing are for _____ which is the uptake of oxygen from environment and the elimination of carbon dioxide from the body.
e: Mechanisms of breathing are for gas exchange which is the uptake of oxygen from environment and the elimination of carbon dioxide from the body. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Circulation is not gas exchange.

q: The general body surface of most animals lacks sufficient _____ to exchange gases for the whole organism.
e: The general body surface of most animals lacks sufficient surface area to exchange gases for the whole organism. A large surface area speeds diffusion, which is why lungs, gills, and leaves are folded or flattened. Mass is not surface area.

q: Aquatic animals that use gills include polychaetes, crustaceans, sea stars and fish, whereas aquatic turtles use _____ for gas exchange.
e: Aquatic animals that use gills include polychaetes, crustaceans, sea stars and fish, whereas aquatic turtles use cloaca for gas exchange. Some vertebrates share a cloaca for digestive, urinary, and reproductive openings. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Gills is different: gills are folded, water-suspended surfaces used by many aquatic animals.

q: Each gill arch has two rows of gill filaments, composed of flattened plates called _____.
e: Each gill arch has two rows of gill filaments, composed of flattened plates called lamellae. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek. Tracheae is not lamellae.

q: The _____ flow of water and blood causes the continuous diffusion of oxygen from the water into the blood over the entire length of a capillary.
e: The counter current flow of water and blood causes the continuous diffusion of oxygen from the water into the blood over the entire length of a capillary. Counter-current flow in fish gills keeps a gradient so more oxygen is extracted. Blood carries oxygen bound to haemoglobin. Cross is not counter current.

q: Some terrestrial animals use tracheae for breathing, such as _____.
e: Some terrestrial animals use tracheae for breathing, such as insects. Many insects breathe through a tracheal system, not lungs. Spiders is not insects.

q: Spiders and scorpions use _____ for breathing.
e: Spiders and scorpions use book lungs for breathing. Book lungs are stacked gas-exchange plates in some arachnids. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange. Gills is different: gills are folded, water-suspended surfaces used by many aquatic animals.

q: Frogs and toads often use the lining of the _____ for gas exchange.
e: Frogs and toads often use the lining of the buccal cavity for gas exchange. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Intestine is not buccal cavity.

q: The lungs are enclosed in the chest or thorax by the rib cage and a muscular sheet of tissue called the _____.
e: The lungs are enclosed in the chest or thorax by the rib cage and a muscular sheet of tissue called the diaphragm. The diaphragm contracts and flattens to increase thorax volume during inhalation. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange. Pericardium is not diaphragm.

q: Joining each rib to the next are two sets of muscles called _____ muscles.
e: Joining each rib to the next are two sets of muscles called intercostal muscles. Intercostal muscles move the ribs to change thorax volume during breathing. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek. Abdominal is not intercostal.

q: The trachea splits into two tubes called the _____, one leading to each lung.
e: The trachea splits into two tubes called the bronchi, one leading to each lung. The trachea is the airway that carries air toward the bronchi. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek. Bronchioles is different: bronchioles are the finer airways that end in alveoli.

q: Each bronchus divides into smaller tubes called bronchioles, eventually ending at microscopic air sacs called _____.
e: Each bronchus divides into smaller tubes called bronchioles, eventually ending at microscopic air sacs called alveoli. Alveoli are tiny lung sacs with a huge surface for diffusion of gases. Bronchioles are the finer airways that end in alveoli. Glomeruli is not alveoli.

q: The walls of trachea and bronchi contain rings of _____ which support the airway and keep them open.
e: The walls of trachea and bronchi contain rings of gristle or cartilage which support the airway and keep them open. Cartilage keeps airways such as the trachea open. The trachea is the airway that carries air toward the bronchi. Bone is not gristle or cartilage.

q: The inside of the thorax is separated from the lungs by two thin, moist membranes called the _____ membranes.
e: The inside of the thorax is separated from the lungs by two thin, moist membranes called the pleural membranes. Pleural membranes and fluid let the lungs slide as the thorax changes volume. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange. Synovial is not pleural.

q: Between the two pleural membranes is a space filled with a thin layer of liquid called _____ fluid.
e: Between the two pleural membranes is a space filled with a thin layer of liquid called pleural fluid. Pleural membranes and fluid let the lungs slide as the thorax changes volume. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek. Serous is not pleural.

q: Some cells in the lining of trachea and bronchi secrete _____ which traps particles of dirt or bacteria.
e: Some cells in the lining of trachea and bronchi secrete mucus which traps particles of dirt or bacteria. Mucus traps particles; cilia sweep that dirt away from the lungs. The trachea is the airway that carries air toward the bronchi. Bile is not mucus.

q: _____ on cells lining the trachea and bronchi prevent the mucus and trapped particles from entering the lungs by beating and sweeping.
e: Cilia on cells lining the trachea and bronchi prevent the mucus and trapped particles from entering the lungs by beating and sweeping. Cilia are tiny beating hairs that move mucus and trapped dust. The trachea is the airway that carries air toward the bronchi. Flagella is not Cilia.

q: During inhalation, the external intercostal muscles _____ and the internal intercostal muscles relax.
e: During inhalation, the external intercostal muscles contract and the internal intercostal muscles relax. Intercostal muscles move the ribs to change thorax volume during breathing. Tear is not contract.

q: During inhalation, the muscles of diaphragm contract and the diaphragm becomes _____.
e: During inhalation, the muscles of diaphragm contract and the diaphragm becomes flattened. The diaphragm contracts and flattens to increase thorax volume during inhalation. Domed is not flattened.

q: During exhalation, the chest _____ in volume and increases in pressure.
e: During exhalation, the chest decreases in volume and increases in pressure. Remains same is not decreases.

q: Ventilation depends on the fact that thorax is an _____ cavity.
e: Ventilation depends on the fact that thorax is an airtight cavity. Ventilation is moving air or water across the gas-exchange surface. Porous is not airtight.

q: The conditions for gas exchange vary depending on whether the breathing medium is air or _____.
e: The conditions for gas exchange vary depending on whether the breathing medium is air or water. Water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Soil is not water.

q: Respiratory organs are extensively folded or branched thereby enlarging the available _____ for gas exchange.
e: Respiratory organs are extensively folded or branched thereby enlarging the available surface area for gas exchange. A large surface area speeds diffusion, which is why lungs, gills, and leaves are folded or flattened. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Weight is not surface area.

q: Marine worms of the phylum Annelida called _____ use gills for gas exchange.
e: Marine worms of the phylum Annelida called polychaetes use gills for gas exchange. Many polychaete worms use gills in water. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide. Nematodes is not polychaetes.

q: Blood flowing through capillaries within the lamellae picks up _____ from the water.
e: Blood flowing through capillaries within the lamellae picks up oxygen from the water. Oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration. Blood carries oxygen bound to haemoglobin. Carbon dioxide is different: carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion.
